sources.entry: OwnTone | Media server for DAAP/iTunes, AirPlay, Chromecast and MPD clients

summary.one_liner: OwnTone is a media server that streams local files, Spotify, pipe input and internet radio to AirPlay, Chromecast, Roku and other receivers, and serves a library over DAAP and RSP.
summary.what_it_does: OwnTone plays audio sources such as local files, Spotify, pipe input and internet radio to AirPlay 1 and 2 receivers, Chromecast receivers, Roku Soundbridge, a browser, or the server's own sound system. Listeners can also connect to it with any client that supports mp3 streaming. Control is available through a web interface, Apple Remote, an Android remote (Retune is named), an MPD client, a JSON API or DACP. It also shares local files over the Digital Audio Access Protocol (DAAP) to iTunes on Windows, Apple Music on macOS and Rhythmbox on Linux, and over the Roku Server Protocol (RSP) to Roku devices. The project was previously called forked-daapd, itself a rewrite of mt-daapd (Firefly Media Server).
use_cases: play local music on AirPlay speakers
share a music library with iTunes or Apple Music clients
control playback from an MPD client
play internet radio on multiple speakers
notable: Sends audio to AirPlay 1 and 2, Chromecast, and Roku Soundbridge receivers from one server
Serves the library over DAAP to iTunes, Apple Music and Rhythmbox, and over RSP to Roku devices
Multiple control options: web interface, MPD, JSON API, DACP, Apple Remote
caveats: The README excerpt gives no install commands; it points to external documentation for installation
Runs on Linux, BSD and macOS only (no Windows platform listed)
